headline_of_day: Nvidia's Huang Exit Rattles Markets as Chip Rivals Gain
dek: Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation wipes out hundreds of billions in Nvidia value and unsettles the AI trade, even as the Dow holds firm.
big_picture: Nvidia's leadership crisis dominates the tape: founder Jensen Huang has resigned amid espionage and conduct allegations, CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO, and the stock has shed roughly $573 billion in value over the past week to close near $162.85. The fallout is rotating capital toward rivals and dragging the broader chip complex lower - AMD fell 8.75% and Broadcom 4.76% even as some investors bought the dip - while the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.22% and the S&P 500 fell 0.40%. The Dow Jones bucked the trend, up 0.10%, as breadth stayed positive (315 advancers to 185 decliners), showing the damage is concentrated in mega-cap tech rather than the broader market. Firmer October producer-price and CPI data, Treasury yields near 5.14%, and a 3.21% jump in the VIX to 19.30 are compounding the risk-off mood ahead of Nvidia's November 17 earnings, now seen as a referendum on the AI trade. Washington infighting over China chip export curbs and Anthropic's trimmed IPO valuation add further uncertainty to the AI-investment narrative.
three_things: Nvidia's Huang is out; interim CEO Kress inherits a stock down ~$573B in a week and a make-or-break earnings report on Nov 17
Chip-sector pain is rotating: AMD and Broadcom sold off hard even as some investors frame the move as a buying opportunity
Inflation data (PPI, CPI) and a rate-hike-leaning Fed are pushing yields and the VIX higher, adding to AI-trade jitters
market_pulse: A mixed, chip-led selloff: the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.22% to 27943.74 and the S&P 500 fell 0.40% to 7561.67, while the Dow Jones bucked the trend to close up 0.10% at 52347.55 and the Russell 2000 slipped 0.31% to 2790.49. Breadth was positive at 315 advancers versus 185 decliners out of 503 S&P names, with damage concentrated in mega-cap tech: Electronic Technology was the weakest sector (-2.11%), while Consumer Non-Durables (+1.45%) and Finance (+0.64%) led gainers. The VIX jumped 3.21% to 19.30, the 10-year yield rose to 5.14%, the dollar gained 0.23% to 103.41, WTI crude eased to 88.56, and Bitcoin tumbled 3.50% to 65843.84.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid espionage and conduct allegations
stories.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has resigned after 33 years, following reports he misled executives about ties to a relative under investigation for potential links to Chinese intelligence, alongside separate allegations of personal misconduct. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and the stock has lost roughly $573 billion in value over the past week to trade near $162.85. Huang is expected to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving, and employees and major shareholders are reportedly pushing for his return.

stories.headline: October inflation data keeps Fed on track for a December rate hike
stories.summary: October's Producer Price Index showed inflation pressures broadening across categories, and Bloomberg reports a firm CPI print is reinforcing the case for the Federal Reserve to raise rates next month. Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson called inflation the most important factor in policy decisions, while Boston Fed President Susan Collins backed a steady, gradual hiking path. The data pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 5.14%.

stories.headline: AMD and Broadcom whipsaw as traders reposition around Nvidia's crisis
stories.summary: AMD and Broadcom initially jumped as investors rotated into Nvidia's rivals following Huang's resignation, with the S&P 500 recovering roughly $1 trillion in value within 90 minutes of an early drop. By Friday's close, however, both stocks sold off sharply - AMD down 8.75% to $534.06 and Broadcom down 4.76% to $347.01 - as the chip sector's volatility continued into the end of the week.

stories.headline: Bessent and Lutnick clash over Nvidia chip export curbs to China
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are reported to be at odds within the Trump administration over how far to restrict advanced Nvidia chip exports to China. The dispute intensifies scrutiny of the export-control agency just as Nvidia navigates its leadership crisis, adding policy uncertainty for semiconductor stocks tied to China demand.

stories.headline: Anthropic trims IPO valuation target to $1.3-$1.4 trillion as AI enthusiasm cools
stories.summary: Anthropic is targeting a $1.3-$1.4 trillion valuation for its IPO, set to begin trading November 19, down from earlier hopes of $1.5-$2 trillion. Underwriters including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley stand to collect roughly $395 million in combined fees, but the offering faces a tougher backdrop than SpaceX's June listing given rising Treasury yields and the Nvidia leadership upheaval.

stories.headline: Microsoft confirms full recovery from global outage that disrupted enterprise clients
stories.summary: Microsoft said its services were fully restored after an outage that paralyzed government offices, traders and businesses worldwide, with some firms reportedly resorting to fax machines during the disruption. A separate major software provider with thousands of Fortune 500 clients reported an outage the same day, renewing questions about concentration risk in enterprise cloud infrastructure.

stories.headline: Micron rebounds nearly 12% on bullish DRAM-shortage calls, but gives back ground into Friday
stories.summary: Micron shares rebounded 11.9% from an early-November selloff after Bernstein reiterated a Buy rating with a $1,300 target and KeyBanc kept an Overweight rating at $1,750, both citing a severe, lasting DRAM shortage with fourth-quarter prices up 15-20%. Micron posted fiscal Q4 revenue of $54.23 billion, up sharply from $11.32 billion a year earlier, with guidance of about $61.5 billion next quarter, though the stock eased 2.52% to $778.31 by Friday's close as chip-sector volatility persisted.

stories.headline: Italy fines Meta €805 million over Android photo-access practices
stories.summary: Italy's Data Protection Authority fined Meta Platforms €805 million (about $887 million) for accessing photos and videos in Android users' galleries without explicit consent. The penalty adds to Meta's mounting regulatory costs in the EU even as the stock rallied 2.90% on the day, bucking broader chip-sector weakness.

stories.headline: Musk pitches Tesla-SpaceX merger as new route to S&P 500 inclusion
stories.summary: Elon Musk is reportedly pitching a Tesla-SpaceX merger as an alternative path for SpaceX to gain S&P 500 index inclusion, reviving a bid that had stalled. The move would be a major corporate restructuring with implications for Tesla shareholders and index-fund flows if pursued; Tesla shares fell 1.82% to $390.22 on the day.

stories.headline: Nationwide ground stop cancels thousands of flights; FAA AI tool denies link
stories.summary: A Friday nationwide ground stop led to thousands of flight cancellations, with disruptions continuing into Saturday. An AI company tied to the FAA's SMART tool denied its software was linked to the outage, as investigators continue to probe the cause.

stories.headline: China's securities regulator warns of global asset-repricing risk amid geopolitical tension
stories.summary: The chairman of China's CSRC warned that rising geopolitical tensions are driving a rebalancing of capital and raising risks of global asset repricing. The comments come as the newly formed US-China trade council held its first video meeting on Friday to discuss tariffs.

stories.headline: Cisco tops estimates, forecasts AI infrastructure revenue to double this fiscal year
stories.summary: Cisco reported quarterly earnings that beat analyst expectations and said it expects AI infrastructure-related revenue to roughly double in the current fiscal year. The guidance underscores continued enterprise demand for AI networking gear even as other parts of the AI trade face volatility.
